comparator.name: Environmental Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Current BES2026:105EC credited compulsory common courses+3EC preparation-dependent mathematics/statistics+12EC thesis=120EC common part;30EC selected specialisation and30EC genuine electives complete180listedEC. InterdisciplinaryEnvironmentalChallenges remains the broadest representative formal route. It requires6EC nexus, at least6EC social and6EC natural-science/technology options, and at most6EC optional quantitative work, totalling30. The existing example keeps12EC first-listed social courses and12EC first-listed natural/technology units (renewable energy6, organicchemistry3+environmentalorganic3), plus nexus6. This balanced example is permitted, not a compulsory two-plus-two rule. MathematicsA selectsMAT14803; MathematicsB selectsStatistics1 with study advice. Thesis requires102BEScredits including all60B1 and the specialisation preparation for the chosen eligible chairgroup. The current public record does not identify which chairgroup accepts this exact combination or its complete preparatory set; that essential progression gate remains unresolved. The official systems-analysis education alternative refers to a Brightspace thesisguide; older environmental-policy/economics guides and MSc-only conditions do not establish this cohort rule. Listed credits/route substance remain usable, not a certified complete pathway. Practical safety0EC is recorded separately; elective internships12/18 replace electives rather than add credits.
components: General, laboratory and fieldwork safety are non-credit requirements for the relevant practical activities. They are not added to the 180 EC.
Sustainability Transitions: Past, Present and Future
Global Production-Consumption Systems and the Environment

WUR studies pollutant emissions, atmospheric transport, chemical conversion, deposition and health effects with models and observations. General climate-change study does not reproduce this air-quality sequence.
The Skills Academy connects programme experiences through personal leadership, reflection and a progress portfolio. A general research project is not its direct equivalent.
Systems of Change: Environmental Policy, Economics, and Law
System Earth: Climate and Global Change

WUR teaches microbial cells, growth and metabolism alongside chemical toxicity, risk assessment and a microbiology practical. Introductory life science at UCR is not the same specialist laboratory and toxicology sequence.

WUR requires a 12 EC international, field-based transdisciplinary project with a commissioner and local stakeholders. It assumes at least 60 EC from the first two years and requires fieldwork safety. Separate UCR projects do not reproduce this coordinated course.
This example uses Mathematics Applied: Introduction for VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; the choice follows prior preparation and study advice.
From Synergies to Trade-Offs at the Pollution-Climate-Biodiversity Nexus

The selected specialisation combines this 6 EC nexus course with 12 EC of social-science and 12 EC of natural-science/technology options. Other permitted combinations may use 6–18 EC in each of those groups, with up to 6 EC of optional quantitative methods, while keeping 30 EC in total.

This example selects the first two listed social-science options: International and EU Environmental Law and Environmental Economics. This is one permitted choice, not a claim that both are compulsory for every student in the specialisation.

This example selects Renewable Energy Technologies and the paired Organic Chemistry 1 and Environmental Organic Chemistry units from the natural-science/technology group. Laboratory safety applies to the chemistry practicals.

WUR studies organic pollutants, their reactivity, breakdown and environmental stability after Organic Chemistry 1. UCR’s metal recovery and soil-remediation work does not reproduce this dedicated organic-chemistry sequence.

The required individual thesis is 12 EC. Entry requires at least 102 BES credits, all 60 first-year credits, and preparation for the chosen chair group. The applicable chair-group preparation for this course combination still needs confirmation.
Thirty EC remains available for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. An optional 12 or 18 EC internship would use part of this space; no internship is required in this example.

routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor offers four current 30-EC specialisations. The interdisciplinary route most directly represents the programme’s published identity as a mix of natural, social and technological sciences, and is selected independently of UCR fit.

core: Environmental systems linking atmosphere, water, soil, ecosystems and human activity
Scientific research, chemistry, mathematics, statistics, modelling and environmental evidence
Climate change, pollution, resource scarcity and sustainability transitions
adjacent: Environmental quality, ecology and resilient ecosystems
Environmental policy, economics, law and governance
Environmental technology, circular resources and sustainable energy
Geo-information, environmental data and spatial resource management
questions: How do human activities and natural processes cause environmental degradation?
How can environmental quality and ecosystem resilience be protected?
Which policy, technological and governance solutions enable sustainable transitions?

alternatives.label: Environmental systems, circular solutions & governance
alternatives.labelReason: Integrate environmental mechanisms in climate, soil, water and ecosystems with quantitative evidence, life-cycle/circular-resource analysis, energy solutions and the economics/governance/communication of environmental responses.
alternatives.concept: Integrate environmental mechanisms in climate, soil, water and ecosystems with quantitative evidence, life-cycle/circular-resource analysis, energy solutions and the economics/governance/communication of environmental responses.
progression: All formal prerequisites precede the dependent course and every fixed-term offering is X. Sustainability and statistical foundations precede specialist environmental chemistry, public economics/econometrics and resource recovery. Biology precedes evolution/marine study. Earth-system tools may follow the completed sustainability foundation without a separate geology prerequisite. No old offering is restored.

alternatives.concept: Study ecosystem condition and resilience through actual biodiversity, conservation, evolutionary and biological mechanisms, coupled with soil/water science, environmental chemistry, remediation and land-use effects.

alternatives.distinctness: The concept changes emphasis toward actual ecological/biodiversity/conservation and land-use mechanisms, with soil/water quality, rather than the closest programme’s quantitative/economic/communication spine. Against earlier programmes: 10courses/75ECeachway.

alternatives.label: Environmental policy, economics & evidence
alternatives.labelReason: Study how institutions, markets, collective choices and behaviour shape environmental responses. Join actual policy/economic methods, qualitative/quantitative evidence and sustainability communication to a concrete environmental-science and resource/water foundation.
alternatives.concept: Study how institutions, markets, collective choices and behaviour shape environmental responses. Join actual policy/economic methods, qualitative/quantitative evidence and sustainability communication to a concrete environmental-science and resource/water foundation.

Sustainability and statistical foundations precede specialist environmental chemistry, public economics/econometrics and resource recovery. Biology precedes evolution/marine study. Earth-system tools may follow the completed sustainability foundation without a separate geology prerequisite. No old offering is restored.
alternatives.distinctness: The concept changes emphasis toward actual government/market instruments, policy analysis, economic and qualitative/quantitative evidence and sustainability communication, while retaining a real environmental-science/resource-water foundation. Against earlier programmes: 7courses/52.5ECeachway, 12courses/90ECeachway.

trace: Chemical/thermodynamic/mechanical principles, nutrient and carbon boundaries, elementary differential models and laboratory measurement provide direct foundations for Earth-system processes. Its biopolymer experiment is a material-science practical, not hydrological field measurement.

Organismal/phylogenetic diversity, ecological roles, biodiversity indices, identification and data collection/analysis give concrete biosphere knowledge and measurement for Earth-system and ecosystem questions.

Supply/demand, incentives, strategic interaction, consumer choice and production/cost analysis supply concrete economic foundations for environmental instruments and the later public-economics component. The introductory course itself is not specialised environmental economics.

Actual wave physics, optical spectroscopy, chemical analysis, microscopic materials and stress/strain supply physical and chemical methods for geoscience and environmental evidence. The final greenwashing communication project is not integrated Earth-system modelling.

Calculus, optimisation, differential equations, dynamic-model implementation and numerical approximation supply actual quantitative tools for environmental process models. The selected detailed evidence is not a separate linear-algebra sequence.

Research design, measurement, sampling, surveys/experiments, statistical inference and actual team data collection/analysis supply concrete environmental/social-policy evidence skills. No environmental project dataset is guaranteed.

Environmental conditions/resources, ecological population/community dynamics, food webs and ecosystem energy/matter fluxes, including R ecological models and a research project, directly implement the biosphere side of Earth-system interactions. Coupled canopy evapotranspiration/soil transport is not established.

Actual product/process life-cycle assessment, environmental/social/health impacts, resource reuse and cost/revenue appraisal directly support the integrated production-consumption and circularity concept. The integrated LCA project supplies a specific environmental systems method, not generic sustainability breadth.

Greenhouse gases, feedbacks/tipping points, sea-level/ocean/ecological impacts and mitigation/adaptation provide substantive climate-system knowledge. Stakeholder interviews and a climate film do not constitute quantitative atmospheric-dynamics training.

Solar/wind/hydro/geothermal/biomass physics, yield calculations, energy storage and system reliability connect climate-response choices to actual resource constraints. Polysun and mini-grid analyses are energy-system applications, not atmospheric circulation models.
R data cleaning, joins, exploration/visualisation and actual spatial-data workflows provide direct methods for environmental evidence. It does not guarantee a climate or water project.

ArcGIS spatial-data models, projections, queries/transformations, surface analysis and remote-sensing acquisition/image processing directly implement geospatial environmental inquiry and a collaborative environmental case study.

Soil formation/properties/chemistry/biology, shallow aquifers, salinization and seismic/resistivity/electromagnetic surveys directly support soil and subsurface-water investigation. Field/lab measurement is substantial; a full groundwater-flow model sequence is not promised.

Actual delta flooding, freshwater scarcity, salinization, subsidence, pollution and engineered/nature-based responses supply concrete water-management and adaptation study. Site-based Zeeland inquiry differs from dedicated catchment-flow equations and water/atmosphere balance measurement.

Public goods, externalities, collective choice, efficiency/equity, spending and taxation directly support the economic logic of environmental policy instruments. Economic models and evidence appraisal are substantial methods; the course is not a full specialised environmental-economics module.

Aqueous speciation, carbonate/redox/mineral/surface chemistry, weathering and biological controls directly implement environmental biogeochemistry. Laboratory evidence and geochemical equilibrium/speciation models support contamination, remediation and resource questions.

Actual phytoremediation/mycoremediation, soil amendments, chemical leaching and metal-recovery laboratory work support contamination intervention and resource circularity. E-waste/panel recycling is a complementary materials theme; it is not the whole of soil science.

Probability, multivariate distributions, estimation/testing, Bayesian updating and Monte Carlo/Gibbs sampling supply concrete uncertainty and inference methods for observations and models. Applications and software differ from WUR’s introductory applied statistics.

Actual persuasion/framing/ethical communication and community projects on sustainable/circular lifestyles, food, water and energy give a direct environmental-behaviour/communication contribution. Literature/field diaries/reflective inquiry do not guarantee policy impact or a specialist legal qualification.

The description directly supports biosphere/hydrosphere/lithosphere/atmosphere interactions, system modelling, proxies/isotope tracers and past/future climate, with a greenhouse-gas-pathways field trip. These receive full consideration; particular tracer protocols or software are not inferred.

Food/water/energy/climate governance, institutions, power, stakeholders and policy-option appraisal provide specific tools for assessing responses to environmental change. The Zeeland policy project does not substitute for hydrological or geological science.

The description supports technical/economic energy-use assessment, solar/wind/bioenergy choices and a partner report/presentation. This directly applies climate-mitigation questions; it does not supply a meteorological or individual thesis equivalent.

Numerical root finding, integration, ODE and linear/nonlinear-system solvers, error, stability and convergence supply concrete scientific-modelling tools. Broad multivariate PDE/vector-calculus coverage is not inferred.

Biomolecules, cells, enzymes/energy metabolism, DNA/heredity and gene expression supply concrete molecular foundations for the ecological option’s evolution, microbial/biogeochemical and biodiversity study. Biomedical examples are complementary; human disease is not presented as an Earth-system specialism.

Habitat loss/fragmentation, climate impacts, invasive species, conservation priorities and threatened-species assessment provide concrete ecosystem-resilience responses to environmental and land-use pressures.

The available description substantively supports geoscience risk analysis, climate-related/mining disasters, drought and toxic-algal hazards and adaptation. It supplies direct environmental-risk content without invented modelling software or field assessment methods.

The description supports actual environmental-justice and social-movement cases, including anti-colonial/feminist/degrowth perspectives. These provide a specific societal appraisal of environmental interventions and affected communities; not a physical hazard model.

Nature-based infrastructure, coastal/river/estuary management, habitat connectivity and intervention design supply a concrete adaptation application linking physical water risks to ecosystem processes.

Rocks/minerals, sedimentation/facies, structural deformation, stratigraphy and tectonic/geophysical processes directly implement geological Earth science, including field mapping, cross-sections and reconstruction of geological history.

Selection, genetic drift, adaptation, population genetics, phylogeny and biogeography supply specific biological mechanisms for changing communities and biodiversity. They complement ecosystem response and do not substitute for soil/water physics.

Physical/chemical oceanography, primary/secondary production, microbial and estuarine/marine ecosystems, acidification and human impacts support coastal biosphere–water interactions. Marine outreach methods do not establish hydrological instrumentation.

The description supports substantial geoscientific research on nuclear-waste storage, geothermal energy and CO2 capture through literature review, reports and professional presentation. This is direct subsurface/resource inquiry, not documented lowland sedimentary logging or a required bachelor thesis.

Environmental impacts of agriculture, biodiversity/ecosystem effects and comparative appraisal of alternative farming practices directly support land-use, soil/water and biosphere resilience. Its literature project is not a prescribed soil-physics field experiment.

Institutions, representation, interest groups, participation and policy, with actual comparative empirical inquiry, supply concrete mechanisms for comparing environmental governance settings. It is complementary political analysis, not environmental-law training.

Actual uncertainty, behavioural limitations, market efficiency/failure, externalities and government intervention give substantive mechanisms for analysing environmental incentives and regulation. Applications are broader than environmental policy.

EU actors, institutions, agenda setting, legislation/implementation and actual legislative-document/process research support the regional political machinery of environmental governance. A specific environmental bill or legal-doctrinal curriculum is not guaranteed.

The course description fully supports OLS/GLS/instrumental-variable estimation, causal/predictive questions, hypothesis tests and Stata/MonteCarlo work culminating in an empirical paper. These are policy-evaluation/economic evidence methods, not international trade or production-chain content.

The available description directly supports policy-making phases across national/international arenas, a sugar case and policy memos. This is substantive public-policy analysis fully considered despite description-only evidence; environmental law or a particular pollution-policy case is not inferred.

Actual interviews, focus groups, document/visual approaches, coding/thematic interpretation and reflexive team research supply specific methods for stakeholder and policy inquiry. It is not a substitute for the full international environmental field-project course.
blocks: Shared planetary-boundary framing, environmental chemical/physical mechanisms and elementary dynamic models. WUR additionally integrates explicit natural/social-science wicked-case teamwork; UCR has a material-science laboratory project.
Shared calculus, differentiation/integration and differential equations; UCR additionally implements dynamic models and numerical approximations.
Shared research design, descriptive/inferential statistics, regression and data interpretation. UCR includes a team empirical project; WUR has its own applied-inference sequence.

Shared differential-equation/system solution, numerical modelling and evaluation of error/stability. WUR explicitly builds pollutant-fate/transport models in Excel/Python; UCR develops more general numerical methods in Mathematica.
No selected dedicated introductory general-chemistry course; sustainability/geochemistry provides partial ingredients rather than the complete requirement.
No single selected course is aligned merely for generic research skills; WUR combines programme-specific broad-case teamwork, information literacy and introductory data work.
No separate second general-chemistry unit is selected.
Generic applied research or PPD does not reproduce the programme-spanning skills/leadership/reflection portfolio.
Preparation-dependent introductory choice remains separate rather than duplicating MathematicalMethods, already aligned to applied calculus.
Shared Earth-system interactions, climate/global change and system modelling, with proxies/isotope tracers and greenhouse-gas pathways at UCR.

Shared product/process life cycles, extraction-to-disposal/reuse, environmental/social consequences, circularity and cost/revenue appraisal. WUR adds coordinated global production-consumption case work and wider socio-technical integration.
Shared renewable resource/energy conversion, physical yield assessment, storage and system reliability. WUR foregrounds thermodynamic analysis; UCR adds Polysun and mini-grid applications.

Shared physical/chemical resource recovery and soil-remediation technologies with actual leaching/recovery and phytoremediation/mycoremediation laboratory work. WUR additionally develops air/wastewater treatment and reactor/design calculations.
Shared soil formation, texture/structure, water/organic/chemical/biological properties and field/laboratory investigation. UCR additionally studies shallow aquifers and geophysical surveys.
Shared ecological conditions/resources, populations, communities, ecosystems, energy/matter fluxes and human impacts. UCR additionally uses R ecological models.
Water study is distributed across UCR courses; no extra canonical row is forced into this distinct introductory component.
UCR soil/aquifer evidence and water adaptation do not establish WUR’s distinct quantitative water-analysis sequence.
Molecular/cellular foundations and ecological/geochemical study do not reproduce the microbial/toxicological science and specialist microbiology practical.
Shared GIS data models, projections/reference, spatial queries/transformations, terrain analysis, remote-sensing foundations and professional-software case work.

Shared sustainability-transition institutions, policy options, stakeholders and food/water/energy cases. WUR has a broader historical transition-theory sequence; UCR applies governance diagnosis and policy advice.

Shared externalities/market failure, public goods, efficiency/equity and policy intervention. WUR applies environmental-economics theory directly to environmental problems; UCR studies public economics across several sectors.

Shared policy-making phases, institutions and policy responses in national/international arenas. WUR additionally integrates environmental economics, justice and law; UCR’s explicit case is sugar policy.
EarthSystemTools integrates natural Earth compartments; that does not itself establish WUR’s specific socio-environmental stakeholder/system-analysis methods.
General climate forcing/impacts do not reproduce pollutant emissions, atmospheric transport, chemical conversion, deposition and air-quality model/observation practicals.
No selected course guarantees the12EC international field-based transdisciplinary commissioner/stakeholder research cycle.
Ecological energy/matter models alone do not establish WUR’s explicit coupled pollution-climate-biodiversity trade-off, stakeholder and leverage-point analysis.
EU institutions and policy methods are not dedicated international/EU environmental-law doctrine or legal skills.
Metal recovery/soil remediation is not organic-pollutant reactivity, degradation and photochemistry after OrganicChemistry1.
Required12ECindividual thesis has no taught-course equivalent; chair-group preparation remains unresolved. OptionalUCR15ECresearch is additional and outside24courses/180EC.
Genuine30ECelective/minor space remains unassigned; optional internship would replace part of it.

notes.text: The UCR programmes combine actual environmental science, ecological study, circular-resource and energy analysis with governance or policy/economic methods. WUR has a more prescribed general/organic chemistry, air-quality, microbiology/toxicology, engineering and environmental-law sequence, plus coordinated international field research and an individual thesis. UCR’s optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

selection.assessment: Three provisional concepts are supported by actual environmental science and natural/social/technology integration, not only generic sustainability coherence. Sequential ecological and policy/economic candidates have substantive curricular consequences and pass all pairwise floors. The fourth circular-technology family is recorded at the maximum, not rejected for lack of a degree title; its core interests also receive real circular-resource/energy treatment in the closest response. External chair-group thesis preparation remains unresolved, so no completed comparison or final academic approval is certified.

audience.programmeDescription: Environmental Sciences at Wageningen combines natural science, social science and technology to investigate pollution, climate change, resource use and environmental solutions. The programme is taught in English and remains rooted in the natural sciences.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programmes explore environmental problems through integrated science and circular solutions, ecosystem resilience, or policy and economic methods. WUR includes a more prescribed chemistry, air-quality, microbiology/toxicology, engineering and environmental-law sequence. Thesis entry for the selected WUR course combination still needs confirmation.
